From 45424e871abf2a152e247a9cff78359f18dd95c0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Berk Cem Goksel <berkcgoksel@gmail.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Mar 2026 16:38:25 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] ALSA: caiaq: fix stack out-of-bounds read in init_card

The loop creates a whitespace-stripped copy of the card shortname
where `len < sizeof(card->id)` is used for the bounds check. Since
sizeof(card->id) is 16 and the local id buffer is also 16 bytes,
writing 16 non-space characters fills the entire buffer,
overwriting the terminating nullbyte.

When this non-null-terminated string is later passed to
snd_card_set_id() -> copy_valid_id_string(), the function scans
forward with `while (*nid && ...)` and reads past the end of the
stack buffer, reading the contents of the stack.

A USB device with a product name containing many non-ASCII, non-space
characters (e.g. multibyte UTF-8) will reliably trigger this as follows:

  BUG: KASAN: stack-out-of-bounds in copy_valid_id_string
       sound/core/init.c:696 [inline]
  BUG: KASAN: stack-out-of-bounds in snd_card_set_id_no_lock+0x698/0x74c
       sound/core/init.c:718

The off-by-one has been present since commit bafeee5b1f8d ("ALSA:
snd_usb_caiaq: give better shortname") from June 2009 (v2.6.31-rc1),
which first introduced this whitespace-stripping loop. The original
code never accounted for the null terminator when bounding the copy.

Fix this by changing the loop bound to `sizeof(card->id) - 1`,
ensuring at least one byte remains as the null terminator.

Fixes: bafeee5b1f8d ("ALSA: snd_usb_caiaq: give better shortname")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Cc: Andrey Konovalov <andreyknvl@gmail.com>
Reported-by: Berk Cem Goksel <berkcgoksel@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Berk Cem Goksel <berkcgoksel@gmail.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260329133825.581585-1-berkcgoksel@gmail.com
Signed-off-by: Takashi Iwai <tiwai@suse.de>

diff --git a/sound/usb/caiaq/device.c b/sound/usb/caiaq/device.c
index dfd820483849..3a71bab8a477 100644
--- a/sound/usb/caiaq/device.c
+++ b/sound/usb/caiaq/device.c
@@ -488,7 +488,7 @@ static int init_card(struct snd_usb_caiaqdev *cdev)
 		memset(id, 0, sizeof(id));
 
 		for (c = card->shortname, len = 0;
-			*c && len < sizeof(card->id); c++)
+			*c && len < sizeof(card->id) - 1; c++)
 			if (*c != ' ')
 				id[len++] = *c;
 
-- 
2.34.1

The patch fixes a stack out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the ALSA caiaq driver (`sound/usb/caiaq/device.c`). The bug occurs in the `init_card` function, where a whitespace-stripped copy of the card shortname is stored in a local buffer `id`. The original loop condition `len < sizeof(card->id)` allowed copying up to 16 non-space characters, but `id` is also 16 bytes, leaving no room for a null terminator. When this non-null-terminated string is later passed to `snd_card_set_id()`, the function reads beyond the buffer, causing the stack out-of-bounds read. The fix changes the loop bound to `sizeof(card->id) - 1`, ensuring at least one byte is reserved for the null terminator.

Root cause:
Off-by-one error in the loop that copies whitespace-stripped characters from `card->shortname` to the local buffer `id`. The condition `len < sizeof(card->id)` allows copying up to 16 non-space characters into a 16-byte buffer, leaving no room for a null terminator. This non-null-terminated string is later passed to `snd_card_set_id()`, which reads past the buffer boundary, causing a stack out-of-bounds read.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
<text>
for (c = card->shortname, len = 0;
     *c && len < sizeof(card->id); c++)
    if (*c != ' ')
        id[len++] = *c;
</text>
Reason:
The loop copies up to `sizeof(card->id)` (16) non-space characters into the local buffer `id`, which is also 16 bytes. When 16 non-space characters are copied, the null terminator is overwritten. Later, `snd_card_set_id(card, id)` is called with a non-null-terminated string, causing `copy_valid_id_string` to read beyond the buffer, leading to a stack out-of-bounds read.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
<text>
for (c = card->shortname, len = 0;
     *c && len < sizeof(card->id) - 1; c++)
    if (*c != ' ')
        id[len++] = *c;
</text>
Reason:
Changing the bound to `sizeof(card->id) - 1` ensures that at most 15 non-space characters are copied, leaving at least one byte in the `id` buffer for the null terminator (which was zeroed initially). This prevents the stack out-of-bounds read when the string is later used by `snd_card_set_id`.
